summary:
AstroFlame is an SI-powered, cross-platform fire safety intelligence dashboard (Next.js Web + Android App) built to translate decades of NASA microgravity combustion research into actionable design insights for crewed spacecraft, space stations, Lunar/Martian bases, and pressurized rovers.

Using data from all 24 investigations in NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) Combustion Science repository—anchored around 8 core habitable fire-safety datasets (BASS-II, SAFFIRE-I/II, ACME BRE, SAME/SAME-R, FLEX, ACME CFI-G, ACME E-FIELD, and SPICE)—AstroFlame ranks experiments across the Three Pillars of Fire Safety (Prevention, Detection, Suppression). Users can adjust SI ranking weights, switch between five technical audience lenses, compare 0.00g spherical blue diffusion flames against 1.00g buoyant flames, and simulate high-oxygen exploration atmospheres (34% O₂ at 8.2 psia). By making microgravity flammability limits, invisible cool flames, and smoke-coagulation behavior immediately explorable, AstroFlame helps engineers design safer off-world habitat
details:
What AstroFlame Does & How It Works AstroFlame is a responsive, multi-page fire safety decision-support platform that synthesizes, ranks, and visualizes microgravity and partial-gravity combustion experiments from the NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) Data Repository. Its core components include:

  • SI Multi-Attribute Ranking Engine: Dynamically scores and ranks all 24 NASA PSI Combustion Science datasets (highlighting 8 Core Fire-Safety Anchors by default) using user-adjustable weights for habitat flammability relevance, high-O₂ coverage, detection/suppression actionability, partial-gravity transferability, and telemetry depth.
  • Five Audience Lenses: Recalibrates insights and terminology for Aerospace Fire Safety Engineers, Researchers/Data Scientists, Professors/PIs, Graduate Students, and Undergraduate Students.
  • Interactive Flame & Atmosphere Simulators: Features a real-time HTML5 <canvas> comparison of 0.00g molecular-diffusion blue flames, 0.16g Lunar flames, 0.38g Martian flames, and 1.00g buoyant yellow flames, plus an Exploration Atmosphere Simulator testing ISS baselines (21% O₂ @ 14.7 psia), Lunar habitats (34% O₂ @ 8.2 psia), EVA suits (100% O₂ @ 4.3 psia), and ACME CFI-G extreme envelopes (up to 85% O₂).
  • ISS Hardware & Historical Context: Maps experiments to the ISS Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR), Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG), Cygnus free-flyers, historical fire incidents (Apollo 1, Apollo 13, Mir), and NASA terrestrial firefighting spin-offs.

Tools, Languages & Architecture

  • Frontend & Mobile: Next.js 15 (App Router), TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, HTML5 Canvas, Recharts/Chart.js, Lucide Icons, and Capacitor Android (@capacitor/android) for native mobile packaging.
  • Authentication & Cloud Persistence: Firebase Authentication (Google Sign-In, Email/Password for both User and Admin roles) and Cloud Firestore (saved_simulations, custom_rankings, and psi_annotations) enabling cross-device Web-to-Android research sync.
  • SI Integration: Natural-language synthesis console and multi-criteria ranking logic grounded in verified NASA PSI metadata and DOIs.

Benefits, Creativity & Factors Considered

  • Strict Domain Boundary: Focuses strictly on habitable crew environments (spacecraft cabins, stations, Lunar/Martian bases, pressurized rovers) while automatically down-weighting terrestrial engine-efficiency studies and excluding high-velocity rocket/propellant combustion.
  • Key Scientific Factors: Accounts for low-flow ventilation hazards (0.5–5 cm/s in BASS-II), smoke particle coagulation evading 1g ionization detectors (SAME), invisible 500–1000 K cool-flame re-ignition (FLEX, CFI-G), and ±10 kV ion-driven wind partial-gravity proxies (E-FIELD).
  • Clean UX: Uses progressive disclosure (compact summary cards paired with slide-over telemetry drawers) so complex combustion physics remains scannable without visual clutter.
